title: Define non-functional requirements such as SLAs, RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective)
description: Define workload availability SLOs, maximum tolerable data loss (RPO), and recovery time (RTO) before production. Cover pod, node, zone, regional, deletion, and corruption scenarios along with external dependencies. Choose architecture, replication, backup frequency, retention, and recovery capacity from these targets and validate them with measured drills rather than service SLA percentages alone.

documentation.title: Define the BCDR strategy

title: Rehearse disaster recovery and clean-environment rebuilds regularly
description: Rebuild into an isolated recovery environment from infrastructure as code, restore representative backups, and validate application and data integrity. Do not delete production to test recovery. Rehearse node, zone, and regional failures appropriate to the workload, and measure achieved RPO and RTO.
detail: Keep versioned runbooks with recovery order, owners, credentials and break-glass access, DNS and traffic changes, validation gates, rollback, and failback. Test without relying on the failed region's pipelines, registry endpoints, secrets, or monitoring, and record remediation actions after drills.

documentation.title: Schedule and perform DR tests regularly

title: Use Availability Zones if supported in your Azure region
applicability: Availability-sensitive workloads requiring resilience to an intra-region zone failure where the Azure region, node VM sizes, and dependencies support availability zones.
description: Where supported by region and VM SKU, distribute application node pools across availability zones and spread replicas across nodes and zones. Zones are separate datacenter failure domains within a region, not update domains in one datacenter. Align storage redundancy, load balancing, and recovery capacity; a zone-enabled cluster does not automatically make every workload or dependency zone-resilient.

documentation.title: Create an AKS cluster across availability zones

title: Plan for multiregion deployment
applicability: Only workloads whose availability, RPO, RTO, or regulatory requirements require recovery in another region; multiple live regions are not required for every workload.
description: Select active-active, warm standby, or cold recovery from workload RPO/RTO, consistency, cost, and data residency requirements. Validate AKS, VM, storage, network, and quota availability in each target region and provision failover capacity. Region pairing is not mandatory for all architectures, but specific replication and Azure Backup Cross Region Restore capabilities depend on supported paired regions.

documentation.title: Plan for multiregion deployment

title: Create a data replication, recovery, and failback plan
applicability: Stateful workloads and external data dependencies whose RPO and RTO require data recovery or failover across failure domains; regional replication is needed only when regional recovery targets justify it.
description: Inventory persistent volumes and external data services and define supported replication or backup/restore for each according to RPO and RTO. Validate consistency and replication lag against RPO, including write fencing to avoid split-brain during failover. Measure recovery and failback time in drills, including data reconciliation and application restart order. Replication can propagate deletion and corruption and is not a substitute for independently retained backups.

documentation.title: AKS multi-region deployment models
AKS backup and restore support matrix

title: Use Standard or Premium tier for production control-plane uptime SLA
description: Use Standard tier for production cluster management, or Premium when long-term Kubernetes support is required. Standard and Premium include a Kubernetes API server uptime SLA of 99.95% with availability zones or 99.9% without, subject to current service terms. Free tier has no financially backed uptime SLA.
detail: The control-plane SLA is not an end-to-end application availability guarantee. AKS Automatic is preconfigured with Standard tier and also has qualifying pod readiness SLA coverage under separate conditions; workload replicas, topology, storage, networking, and recovery still require design and testing.

title: Spread workload replicas across nodes and zones
applicability: Availability-sensitive workloads that need replicated serving capacity during node or zone failure; apply zone spreading where supported and required by the workload availability target.
description: Use topology spread constraints for kubernetes.io/hostname and topology.kubernetes.io/zone, or justified anti-affinity, to distribute replicas across failure domains. Match label selectors to the intended workload and ensure enough replicas and capacity remain after a domain failure.
detail: Choose maxSkew and DoNotSchedule versus ScheduleAnyway deliberately. Strict rules can leave replacement pods pending when a zone or capacity is unavailable; test their interaction with volume topology, taints, autoscaling, and upgrades. Scheduling constraints do not automatically rebalance every already-running pod.

documentation.title: Pod topology spread constraints

title: If using a private registry (ACR), configure region replication to store images in multiple regions
applicability: Multi-region recovery scenarios where AKS depends on a private registry and required container images must remain accessible during a regional outage.
description: For multi-region AKS deployments, evaluate ACR Premium geo-replication or another tested image-distribution strategy so recovery nodes can pull required digests during a regional outage.
detail: ACR geo-replication is asynchronous and is not an independent backup against deletion or compromise. Confirm required images and OCI artifacts are available before regional rollout, configure private endpoints and DNS for replicas where needed, and test cold-node pulls during failover.

documentation.title: Enable geo-replication for container images

title: Verify registry regional zone support and data-plane resilience
applicability: Deployments using Azure Container Registry where registry availability is part of the workload's zone-resilience requirements.
description: ACR data-plane zone redundancy is enabled by default for all tiers in regions supporting availability zones, including existing registries and supported geo-replicas. Verify region support rather than requiring the legacy zoneRedundancy property to be Enabled; that property no longer controls behavior. ACR Tasks do not currently support availability zones, and zone redundancy does not protect against a region-wide outage.

documentation.title: Zone redundancy in Azure Container Registry

title: Separate the registry lifecycle from disposable compute resources
applicability: Shared or recovery-critical registries whose artifacts must outlive disposable AKS environments.
description: Place shared registries in a resource group whose lifecycle is independent of disposable AKS environments. Apply least-privilege management access and appropriate resource locks to reduce accidental registry deletion.
detail: Resource groups are lifecycle and management scopes, not backup boundaries. Registry resource locks do not prevent all data-plane artifact deletion; protect repository permissions and retain recoverable copies of critical release artifacts.

documentation.title: Registry best practices - Use dedicated resource group

title: Evaluate ACR soft delete preview and compatible artifact recovery controls
applicability: Azure Container Registry deployments evaluating artifact deletion recovery where preview support terms and soft-delete compatibility limitations are acceptable.
description: Where preview use is acceptable, evaluate ACR soft delete with a tested 1-90 day retention and restore process. It currently does not support geo-replicated registries or artifact cache and cannot coexist with the retention policy. Retained artifacts incur storage charges. Use another compatible recovery strategy when these limitations conflict with regional resilience requirements.
detail: Restore tests must include multi-architecture manifests and OCI referrers: restoring a manifest list or subject does not recursively restore child manifests or signatures. Soft delete is not an independent backup against registry deletion or compromise.

documentation.title: Enable soft delete policy

title: Select and test a supported recovery solution for cluster resources and data
applicability: Workloads with Kubernetes resources or durable data that must be recovered after loss, deletion, or corruption. Select coverage per volume type and external data service; Azure Backup-specific requirements apply only when that implementation is selected.
description: Select Azure Backup for AKS or another supported recovery solution that meets measured RPO, RTO, retention, and consistency requirements. Inventory Kubernetes resources, PV types, excluded data, and managed external data services; configure supported protection for each and test restores for data integrity and application readiness. Protect backup resources with a lifecycle independent of disposable clusters and source data. Document dependencies on snapshots, metadata, source accounts, and regions rather than treating replication or successful backup jobs as proof of recoverability.
detail: When using Azure Backup, Operational backups use snapshots and extension metadata storage in your subscription; eligible Azure Disk backups can also transfer to the Vault tier, but a Backup vault does not mean all backup data is vaulted. Check the live support matrix: Azure Files SMB requires CSI driver 1.32+, is Operational-tier only with at most 30-day retention, and has network, file-count, and restore-location restrictions. NFS Files, Blob CSI, Azure Container Storage, and in-tree PVs are not covered. Enable CSI snapshots, supported managed identities, a healthy Linux backup extension, Trusted Access, and required networking/RBAC; don't co-install Velero with that extension. Snapshot backups are crash-consistent, not automatically application-consistent or atomic across volumes; use supported application hooks or database-native protection when needed. Protect excluded resources and external services separately and validate that source deletion cannot remove the only recovery copy.

documentation.title: Azure Backup for AKS
Back up Azure Kubernetes Service using Azure Backup
AKS backup support matrix and limitations

title: Match backup tiers and cross-region restore to measured RPO and RTO
applicability: Only deployments selecting Azure Backup for AKS; assess Vault tier and Cross Region Restore only when their supported scenarios are needed to meet recovery requirements.
description: Validate backup cadence, completion, tiering, replication lag, and restore duration against recovery targets. Operational AKS backups have a minimum scheduled interval of four hours and restore within the source region. Vault-tier recovery points are daily for eligible Azure Disks; Cross Region Restore requires supported paired regions, a geo-redundant Backup vault, and Cross Region Restore enabled.
detail: The current matrix describes up to 24-hour primary-region and up to 36-hour secondary-region vaulted RPO, not continuous point-in-time recovery. Vaulting is region-limited and currently supports at most 100 Azure Disk PVs per backup instance with disks no larger than 1 TB, public disk network access enabled, and no Disk Encryption Set or Microsoft Entra data-access authentication. Azure Files is not eligible. Do not weaken required security controls simply to enable vaulting; choose another supported recovery strategy when necessary. Test target-cluster capacity, compatible APIs, identities, networking, recovery order, and cleanup of staged restore resources.

documentation.title: Vaulted backup and Cross Region Restore limitations

title: Protect recovery points from deletion and monitor restore readiness
applicability: Only deployments using Azure Backup for AKS. For other recovery implementations, assess equivalent deletion protection, monitoring, and restore readiness under the recovery-solution control.
description: Separate backup administration from workload administration and evaluate supported vault immutability, enhanced soft delete, and multi-user authorization. Alert on backup failures, skipped volumes, stale recovery points, and vault-tier transfer failures. Validate restore permissions and recovery-point usability through drills.
detail: Vault protections do not automatically protect Operational-tier snapshots or extension metadata in your subscription. Azure Files snapshots depend on the source share and account lifecycle. Confirm supported resource-lock behavior, deletion permissions, and retention for each storage type rather than treating successful configuration as ransomware protection.

documentation.title: AKS backup supported protection features and limitations

title: Configure disruption budgets and test maintenance capacity
applicability: Replicated availability-sensitive workloads managed through the Eviction API during drains, upgrades, or consolidation; not a blanket requirement for restartable batch jobs or workloads that deliberately accept interruption.
description: Create separate policy/v1 PodDisruptionBudget objects with selectors matching replicated services and tested minAvailable or maxUnavailable values. Verify healthy replicas, allowed disruptions, and spare scheduling capacity so drains and upgrades can progress within the workload availability target. Test eviction behavior with unhealthy pods and measure drain completion time; configure readiness, rollout strategy, replicas, and topology separately.
detail: PDBs constrain voluntary Eviction API operations such as normal node drains, not hardware or zone failures, direct pod deletion, or Deployment and StatefulSet rolling updates. Involuntary disruptions can reduce the remaining disruption allowance but aren't prevented by the budget. A zero-disruption budget can block maintenance; permit at least one eviction where the workload allows it and document coordination when it doesn't. Consider unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow when an unhealthy pod would otherwise block draining, and test that policy against application recovery behavior. A PDB isn't an uptime guarantee.
